app_summary: An online shop selling astronomy products, based on the OpenTelemetry Demo. It is built with polyglot microservices (Go, Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, Rust, ...) communicating via gRPC and HTTP behind an Envoy frontend-proxy, with Kafka for asynchronous order processing and Valkey as cart store. Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

final_report.root_cause: A routing misconfiguration in the Envoy proxy (frontend-proxy) caused several upstream route/cluster entries to incorrectly resolve to the frontend service, so outbound calls from frontend were routed back through the proxy to frontend again. This produced a recursive frontend <-> frontend-proxy request loop that manifested as repeated alternating spans in traces and ~15s end-to-end latencies.
final_report.evidence_summary: 1) Trace evidence: ~30 slow/error traces show repeated alternating hops between frontend and frontend-proxy (examples: traceID=55e62fbe3cfc2bd80dbf453f67e1abf9 latency_ms=16006.341 sequence='frontend -> frontend-proxy -> frontend -> ...'; traceID=a094acb8d841777c8fbdd266dcaa4d8c latency_ms=15071.71 sequence='frontend-proxy -> frontend -> frontend-proxy -> ...'). These traces consistently show ~15s latency and has_error=true with error_message='N/A', consistent with infinite/long request cycling rather than an upstream HTTP error. 2) Envoy runtime logs: frontend-proxy logs show Envoy bootstrap and routing runtime active (e.g., 'loading 13 cluster(s)', 'loading 1 listener(s)', 'all clusters initialized', admin at 0.0.0.0:10000), confirming Envoy had clusters/routes loaded at runtime. 3) Kubernetes configuration: frontend-proxy pod environment sets FRONTEND_HOST=frontend and FRONTEND_PORT=8080 and the frontend Service and frontend pod both expose port 8080 with matching Endpoints (10.244.1.35:8080) — i.e., the frontend service and pod are healthy and correctly configured, ruling out a two-sided port/name mismatch.
final_report.investigation_summary: High-priority trace analysis (get_traces) revealed consistent recursive frontend <-> frontend-proxy spans and ~15s latencies. Envoy runtime logs (get_logs) were inspected and show Envoy clusters/listeners initialized, indicating Envoy was actively routing. Kubernetes resource descriptions (kubectl describe) confirmed the frontend Service and pod ports match the proxy's target environment (FRONTEND_HOST/PORT), so there is no service-port mismatch on the frontend side. Correlating these items supports the conclusion that Envoy's route/cluster configuration contained incorrect upstream mappings that routed backend-targeted requests back to the frontend cluster, causing the observed recursive loop. No evidence was found that frontend itself was mis-declared or unhealthy; the fault is localized to frontend-proxy's routing behavior.
